chapter: Glen Island, early records and Duke Ellington
title: Glen Island Casino: the all-New York band and interference
summary: To meet union rules he had to replace out-of-town musicians for the Glen Island Casino, where management dictated repertoire and compared him to Casa Loma.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Well, again Milton Romer to the front. He worked out of -- I guess he didn't give up on me. He got me the job at the Glen Island Casino. Now, I had this band that I'd been rehearsing, and you know, doing some work around, a little work around with it, and it was a travelling band, and by that, they weren't all Local 802 members. Excuse me. And when we had to go into the Glen Island Casino, the pay was so poor that you used to have to pay an extra 30 percent if you were a travelling band. And the pay was so poor that he says, "No, you've got to have an all New York band here or you're not going to make it." And so I had to get rid of a wonderful trumpet player by the name of Frank Amerall, and along with some other guys, and change it to an all New York band, and consequently when the band opened there, it was nothing like the band that we had had. And there was a lot of interference in that whole operation.

Dictation of what was to be played and what was not to be played and who was going to make the arrangements and who was going to sing and who wasn't, and it wasn't a particularly happy engagement at all. And then we were standing in the shade of how great the Casa Loma Band had been, and the Dorsey Brothers, and -- there again, I could be wrong. I was more conscious of the Casa Loma Band. Maybe the Dorsey Brothers hadn't been there yet. I

don't know. It's possible they hadn't. But definitely the Casa Loma Band had really exploded there, and everything was, "Why don't you do it like the Casa Loma Band did?" You know this is pretty hard to live under. So that we finished out there and we were very happy.
